title: environment detection response chain
question: What must occur after a sensor or utility control detects a threat for the protected room, media, evidence, or service to remain safe and available?
scenario: Evidence archive room: An incident-response team stores removable evidence media in a small room shared with general IT supplies.
focalRelation: Prevention and environmental capacity reduce exposure; detection must notify an accountable responder; containment/suppression depends on people and life safety; power and HVAC resilience depend on transfer, fuel, maintenance, testing, and upstream utilities; recovery verifies readiness.

nodes.label: Environmental Threat
nodes.detail: Fire, water, temperature, humidity, smoke, or power loss can damage the evidence archive and its custody records.

nodes.label: Sensor Or Prevention Control
nodes.detail: Detection, suppression, containment, power, and environmental controls are selected for the credible hazard.

nodes.label: Alarm Event
nodes.detail: A threshold breach creates a time-stamped alarm with location, condition, and severity.

nodes.label: Accountable Responder
nodes.detail: A named role receives the alarm, protects people and evidence, and records the response outcome.

nodes.label: Generator Capability
nodes.detail: The generator must support the critical evidence-room load for the required duration.

nodes.label: Transfer, Fuel And Maintenance
nodes.detail: Automatic transfer, fuel supply, preventive maintenance, alarms, and load tests determine usable generator capability.

prediction.prompt: What must occur after a sensor or utility control detects a threat for the protected room, media, evidence, or service to remain safe and available?

options.label: Accept the generator because its nameplate capacity exceeds the average building load.
options.feedback: Average capacity does not prove transfer behavior, starting load, runtime, fuel, maintenance, or dependency coverage.

options.label: Connect detection to accountable response, safe containment, continuity, recovery, and verified readiness.
options.feedback: An alarm, generator, secure room, or suppression system is only one component; availability and custody depend on maintained and tested response chains.

options.label: Redundant power equipment automatically proves service availability.
options.feedback: Capacity, transfer, runtime, fuel, maintenance, dependencies, alarms, and load tests determine whether the end-to-end path works.

prediction.hint: A standby component is not a capability until transfer, load, runtime, and failure behavior are tested.

retry.prompt: Removable incident evidence is stored in a room shared with general IT supplies, and many support staff can enter. Which correction addresses the evidence risk?

options.label: Separate evidence storage, restrict and log access, maintain inventory, and monitor environmental conditions
options.feedback: Correct. The control set protects custody, access, integrity, retention, and the storage environment together.

options.label: Add another UPS because evidence custody is primarily an electrical-availability problem
options.feedback: Power matters, but the changed case centers on access, custody, inventory, and environmental separation.

options.label: Keep the shared room and rely on a label attached to each evidence item
options.feedback: Labels do not restrict entry, establish custody, reconcile inventory, or protect the storage environment.

retry.hint: Prefer verified critical-load performance over a nameplate capacity claim.

takeaway: Use the case evidence to apply this relation: Prevention and environmental capacity reduce exposure; detection must notify an accountable responder; containment/suppression depends on people and life safety; power and HVAC resilience depend on transfer, fuel, maintenance, testing, and upstream utilities; recovery verifies readiness.
assumptions: Only entities and claims anchored in the canonical unit or explicitly labeled hypothetical scenario are used.
A highlighted path means the learner is inspecting that path; it does not assert the event occurred.
The current source is authoritative for facts; this treatment reorganizes presentation without changing canonical content.
The lesson teaches one bounded decision and does not claim to exhaust every jurisdiction, vendor implementation, architecture, attack, or exception.

treatmentDispositions.rationale: The comparison links an environmental threat to prevention or sensing, alarm, accountable response, and the generator chain of transfer, fuel, maintenance, and representative-load testing. It preserves detection-to-response and utility evidence for an evidence archive; separate wiring-closet, data-center, and work-area cases remain canonical reference content.

learningJob.plainExplanation: A sensor or redundant component is useful only when it triggers accountable response and works through the full dependency chain. Generator nameplate capacity does not prove transfer, starting load, runtime, fuel, alarms, or maintenance.
learningJob.visualReasoningGain: A hazard-to-response-and-recovery matrix would add coordinated layer and evidence comparison; the current paired cards add only selected dependencies.
